evaluation.verdict: Useful for the admitted route and new item progression; keep using these actions. This is a controlled state-aware player, not autonomous pathfinding or a full game solver.
evaluation.comparison: Existing approach already reached inventory/deposit and terminal entry. New work reuses those facts and adds per-action success, map/HP/inactive guards, frame bounds, goal-driven cursor/navigation, exact input records and localized failures. Two sealed provision cold runs need zero inside-run interventions; no historical agent-time speedup is claimed.
evaluation.development_effort: One failed card selection and two failed navigation versions exposed actionable timing/budget issues; two composition errors were also refused. Those failures are retained, not counted as progression.
evaluation.new_milestone_cost: The second inventory column/row, card storage and sonicdriver acquisition reuse the same cursor/select actions, with no new framework mechanism or memory watches. One provisioning cold run completed after the composition fixes, then two final cold replays matched.
evaluation.timing_scope: Recorded wall seconds cover actual run_session only; exclude analysis, route development, compilation preparation and agent time. No comparable historical timing dataset exists.
scope_limits: Plans have specific waypoints and game-state assumptions; they do not choose new mission objectives or route around arbitrary terrain.
Healthy route expectsHP95 and inactivebit clear. Unexpected damage is refused; no healing/combat policy is implemented.

Goals sample at byte-verified original PCs, bounded by visits and emulated frames plus wall timeout. A frame budget ending away from an expectedPC captures diagnostic snapshots, not a success or access event.
Recorded inputs are acknowledged control changes at paused PC/frame/CCK anchors, not every internal hardware poll.
Checkpoint development runs are separate from final continuous cold-boot progression. The original direct-payload launch is retained; original disk/loader parity remains unproved.
Engineer isID$32; development logs incorrectly said LtCommander, which is$31. No canonical source fact was changed to that wrong name.
Terminal has a held-ID redraw, not a separate submit command. Cache50 and completion at9078 establish display path; they do not establish mission success or all security permissions.

Private ROM/media/raw reports/guest checkpoints stay out of published commits. No target source/fact output change or new byte purpose follows.
